en.greeting: Hi! You already say dibangun, dicuci and dikirim every day. Today you learn the English passive: be + the third form, by for the doer, and when to use it. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: be + the third form
steps.text: Indonesian has a passive you use every day: dibangun, dicuci, dikirim. English has one too.
steps.body:
The **passive** starts with the thing that **receives** the action: *The office is cleaned every day* (dibersihkan). **di- ≈ be + third form** (the past participle from the present perfect).
- **Present: am/is/are + third form**, for routines and facts.
- **Past: was/were + third form**, for finished events.
*di-* never shows the time or how many, but English must choose: **is/are** or **was/were**, singular or plural, for the new **subject** (the word before the verb).

steps.title: The passive in real life
steps.text: Look at be in each sentence: it shows the time and agrees with the thing.
steps.body: **I was born in Medan** is a passive you already know. Indonesian *lahir* has no di-, so don't forget **was**: not 'I born in Medan'.

examples.en: The rooms are cleaned every morning.
This dish is called rendang.
English is spoken in many countries.
examples.id: Bahasa Inggris dipakai di banyak negara.

examples.en: Borobudur was built in the 9th century.
The tickets were sold in one hour.
I was born in Medan.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A factory in Karawang makes motorbikes every day.

question.explanation: The motorbikes don't make anything: they **are made** (dibuat). A fact about now and plural motorbikes → **are** + third form **made**. 'made' alone has no be, and 'are make' uses the base form.

steps.title: Two traps
steps.text: Two mistakes Indonesian speakers often make with the passive, and why they're wrong.
steps.body:
**1. No be.** 'The office cleaned every day' says the **office** did the cleaning (cleaned looks like the past simple). The office doesn't clean: it **is cleaned**. *di-* = **be** + third form, so you need both. And **is cleaning** (be + -ing) means the subject is doing it now.
**2. The past, not the third form.** After be you need the third form: 'was build' → **was built**, 'was wrote' → **was written**. These irregular third forms are new: learn them.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina is showing you the pictures from her wedding last month.

question.prompt: Complete: These photos ___ at Rina's wedding.
question.explanation: A finished event and plural photos → **were**, then the third form: take → took → **taken**. 'were took' uses the past form, and 'taken' alone has no be.

steps.title: by + the doer
steps.text: Want to say who did it? Indonesian uses oleh. English uses by.
steps.body: Put **by + the doer** after the verb: *Bumi Manusia was written **by** Pramoedya.* **by = oleh**. **Trap:** not **from**. **from = dari** says where something **comes from** (*a letter from Budi*); **by** says **who did it**. So 'written from Pramoedya' is wrong. After by, use **me, him, her, us, them** (not 'by she'). **made in** = the place, **made by** = the maker.

pairs.en: by me / him / her / us / them
pairs.id: oleh saya / dia / dia / kami / mereka

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Sari is proud of her family's sambal recipe.

question.solution: This sambal is made by my grandmother.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Sambal ini dibuat oleh nenekku.
question.explanation: The thing comes first: **This sambal**. Then **is made** (a fact about now: be + third form) and **by** (= oleh) + the doer: **my grandmother**.

steps.title: When is the passive better?
steps.text: English uses the active most of the time. So when do you choose the passive?
steps.body: Choose the **passive** when the doer is **unknown** (*My phone was stolen*), **obvious** (*The rubbish is collected on Mondays*; rubbish is British, Americans say trash) or **unimportant**, or when the **thing is the topic** (*Rice is grown in Java*). Then leave out by: 'by someone' adds nothing. Choose the **active** when the doer matters, especially when it's **you**: Indonesian says *Bajunya sudah saya cuci*, but English says **I've washed the clothes**, not 'The clothes were washed by me'.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Your manager asks: 'What did you do yesterday afternoon?' You want to say 'Laporannya saya selesaikan.'

options: The report was finished by me.
question.prompt: Which answer sounds natural in English?
question.explanation: The doer is **you** and that's the point of the answer, so English uses the **active**: **I finished the report.** 'was finished by me' is grammatical but sounds strange in English, and 'The report finished by me' has no be.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip through these cards to lock in the form, the new third forms and by.

steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · passive (present & past)
artifact.intro: Passive = am/is/are + third form (now, always) or was/were + third form (finished). di- ≈ be + third form, oleh = by.
tips: Never drop **be**: **The office is cleaned**, not 'The office cleaned'. After be, the **third form**: **was built**, not 'was build'.
**by** (= oleh) + the doer: **written by Pramoedya**, not 'from Pramoedya'. After by: me, him, her, us, them.
Passive when the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant (usually no by). Active when the doer matters, especially **I**: **I made it**, not 'It was made by me'.

id.greeting: Hai! Kamu sudah bilang dibangun, dicuci dan dikirim setiap hari. Hari ini kamu belajar passive dalam bahasa Inggris: be + bentuk ketiga, by untuk pelaku, dan kapan memakainya. Yuk, langkah demi langkah.

steps.title: be + bentuk ketiga
steps.text: Bahasa Indonesia punya bentuk pasif yang kamu pakai setiap hari: dibangun, dicuci, dikirim. Bahasa Inggris juga punya.
steps.body:
**Passive** dimulai dengan benda yang **dikenai** tindakan: *The office is cleaned every day* (dibersihkan). **di- ≈ be + bentuk ketiga** (past participle dari present perfect).
- **Present: am/is/are + bentuk ketiga**, untuk kebiasaan dan fakta.
- **Past: was/were + bentuk ketiga**, untuk kejadian yang sudah selesai.
*di-* tidak menunjukkan waktu atau jumlah, tapi bahasa Inggris harus memilih: **is/are** atau **was/were**, tunggal atau jamak, sesuai **subjek** barunya (kata sebelum kata kerja).

steps.title: Passive dalam kehidupan sehari-hari
steps.text: Perhatikan be di setiap kalimat: be menunjukkan waktu dan menyesuaikan dengan bendanya.
steps.body: **I was born in Medan** adalah passive yang sudah kamu kenal. *Lahir* tidak memakai di-, jadi jangan lupa **was**: bukan 'I born in Medan'.

examples.en: The rooms are cleaned every morning.
This dish is called rendang.
English is spoken in many countries.
examples.id: Bahasa Inggris dipakai di banyak negara.

examples.en: Borobudur was built in the 9th century.
The tickets were sold in one hour.
I was born in Medan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sebuah pabrik di Karawang membuat sepeda motor setiap hari.

question.explanation: Sepeda motornya tidak membuat apa-apa: sepeda motornya **are made** (dibuat). Fakta tentang sekarang dan motorbikes jamak → **are** + bentuk ketiga **made**. 'made' saja tidak punya be, dan 'are make' memakai bentuk dasar.

steps.title: Dua jebakan
steps.text: Dua kesalahan yang sering dibuat penutur bahasa Indonesia dengan passive, dan kenapa salah.
steps.body:
**1. Tanpa be.** 'The office cleaned every day' berarti **kantornya** yang membersihkan (cleaned terlihat seperti past simple). Kantor tidak membersihkan: kantor **is cleaned**. *di-* = **be** + bentuk ketiga, jadi kamu perlu dua-duanya. Dan **is cleaning** (be + -ing) berarti subjeknya sedang melakukannya.
**2. Bentuk lampau, bukan bentuk ketiga.** Setelah be kamu perlu bentuk ketiga: 'was build' → **was built**, 'was wrote' → **was written**. Bentuk ketiga tidak beraturan ini baru: hafalkan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina menunjukkan foto-foto pernikahannya bulan lalu.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: These photos ___ at Rina's wedding.
question.explanation: Kejadian yang sudah selesai dan photos jamak → **were**, lalu bentuk ketiga: take → took → **taken**. 'were took' memakai bentuk lampau, dan 'taken' saja tidak punya be.

steps.title: by + pelaku
steps.text: Mau menyebut siapa pelakunya? Bahasa Indonesia memakai oleh. Bahasa Inggris memakai by.
steps.body: Taruh **by + pelaku** setelah kata kerjanya: *Bumi Manusia was written **by** Pramoedya.* **by = oleh**. **Jebakan:** bukan **from**. **from = dari** menunjukkan **asal** sesuatu (*a letter from Budi*); **by** menunjukkan **siapa pelakunya**. Jadi 'written from Pramoedya' itu salah. Setelah by, pakai **me, him, her, us, them** (bukan 'by she'). **made in** = tempatnya, **made by** = pembuatnya.

pairs.en: by me / him / her / us / them
pairs.id: oleh saya / dia / dia / kami / mereka

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sari bangga dengan resep sambal keluarganya.

question.solution: This sambal is made by my grandmother.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Sambal ini dibuat oleh nenekku.
question.explanation: Bendanya di depan: **This sambal**. Lalu **is made** (fakta tentang sekarang: be + bentuk ketiga) dan **by** (= oleh) + pelakunya: **my grandmother**.

steps.title: Kapan passive lebih tepat?
steps.text: Bahasa Inggris lebih sering memakai kalimat aktif. Jadi kapan kamu memilih passive?
steps.body: Pilih **passive** kalau pelakunya **tidak diketahui** (*My phone was stolen*), **sudah jelas** (*The rubbish is collected on Mondays*; rubbish itu British, orang Amerika bilang trash) atau **tidak penting**, atau kalau **bendanya yang jadi topik** (*Rice is grown in Java*). Kalau begitu, by tidak perlu: 'by someone' tidak menambah informasi. Pilih **aktif** kalau pelakunya penting, terutama kalau pelakunya **kamu sendiri**: dalam bahasa Indonesia *Bajunya sudah saya cuci*, tapi bahasa Inggris bilang **I've washed the clothes**, bukan 'The clothes were washed by me'.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Manajermu bertanya: 'What did you do yesterday afternoon?' Kamu mau bilang 'Laporannya saya selesaikan.'

options: The report was finished by me.
question.prompt: Jawaban mana yang terdengar wajar dalam bahasa Inggris?
question.explanation: Pelakunya **kamu sendiri** dan itulah inti jawabannya, jadi bahasa Inggris memakai kalimat **aktif**: **I finished the report.** 'was finished by me' memang benar secara tata bahasa tapi terdengar aneh dalam bahasa Inggris, dan 'The report finished by me' tidak punya be.
